headline: Open tools automate quantitative measurement of cell and tissue images
label: Open Source Bioimage Quantification Software
summary: Recent open-source releases automate quantification across scratch assays, 3D mitochondrial networks, vessels, and holographic images.
synthesis: The dominant thread is open, scriptable software that automates quantitative extraction from microscopy data. InVitroGap, an open-source Python tool, automates wound-closure quantification in scratch assays and reports agreement with IncuCyte (R² 0.964–0.983). MitoGraph-GPU accelerates three-dimensional mitochondrial network segmentation using CuPy-vectorized Hessian filtering, with up to 30× speedup on lattice light-sheet data. PAVSAT combines YOLOv8 segmentation, skeletonization, graph analysis, and overlapping tiling to quantify vessel diameters. HoloBio provides an open-source Python GUI for holographic microscopy with real-time and offline processing, cell tracking, and phase and thickness analysis. The distinctive element is GPU acceleration and deep-learning segmentation applied within openly distributed tools for routine morphological readouts. The items do not share a common validation standard; only InVitroGap reports agreement against a reference platform.
